title: Permutations and combinations
overview: Count arrangements (order matters) and selections (order doesn't) using factorials, permutations and combinations. This guide turns the current syllabus outcomes into a connected revision sequence: learn the ideas, practise the method, then use the recall cards and checklist to diagnose what still needs work.
syllabusPoints: Handle adjacency, separation and positional restrictions.
Use complementary counting and gap methods.

definitions.definition: Objects whose interchange creates no new arrangement.
Counting all outcomes then subtracting forbidden outcomes.

sections.title: Order versus selection
content: Use ⁿPᵣ=n!/(n−r)! when order matters and ⁿCᵣ=n!/[r!(n−r)!] when it does not. Many problems combine a selection stage with a later arrangement stage; multiply the stage counts.
bullets: Ask whether swapping two chosen objects changes the outcome.
Explain each factor instead of presenting an unexplained product.

sections.title: Repeated objects
content: For n objects with repeated groups of sizes a,b,…, the number of distinct linear arrangements is n!/(a!b!…). Dividing removes permutations that look identical.
bullets: Count the total number of letters carefully.
Only divide for genuinely identical objects.

sections.title: Objects together or apart
content: For objects that must stay together, treat the block as one object and multiply by internal orders. For 'not together', subtract together-cases from all arrangements. For separated identical objects, arrange the other objects and place them in gaps.
bullets: A block can appear in more than one internal order.
Gap methods need enough available gaps.

sections.title: Position and grouping restrictions
content: Handle fixed positions first, then arrange remaining objects. For rows or teams, select who occupies a group and then arrange within it if positions are distinct. Watch for double-counting when groups themselves are unlabelled.
bullets: Circular arrangements are outside this syllabus.
Cases should be mutually exclusive before adding.

examTips: Annotate products with short labels such as choose, arrange and internal order.
Check whether groups or positions are labelled before deciding about division.
Show the mathematical setup and exact working before the final rounded answer; unsupported calculator output may not earn method marks.
commonMistakes: Using permutations for a selection with no order.
Forgetting internal arrangements of a block.
Adding cases that overlap and double-count outcomes.

quickRecall.question: When is ⁿCᵣ appropriate?
quickRecall.answer: When selecting r objects and the order of selection does not matter.

quickRecall.question: How do you count arrangements where A and B stay together?
quickRecall.answer: Treat AB as one block, arrange the blocks, then multiply by 2 for AB or BA.

quickRecall.question: How is 'A and B not together' often counted?
quickRecall.answer: All arrangements minus arrangements in which they form a block.

quickRecall.question: Why divide by a! for a identical objects?
quickRecall.answer: Their a! internal permutations produce no visibly different arrangement.
